items.title: Make strict completion the shared default for every streaming provider
securityTests: T1 truncated stream succeeds as providerDone
items.rationale: roadmap 0.2.1 item 1: openAIChatEvents/createOpenAICompatibleProvider default strictCompletion to false-undefined, so azure/bedrock/vertex/openrouter/zai/neuralwatt (all six stream through the shared base without the flag) accept EOF without [DONE]/finish_reason as successful providerDone (enforcement exists at openai-compatible.ts:136 and never fires). Fix: flip the shared default to true; existing strictCompletion: false stays honored as the documented opt-out (Task 0 decision 1); alibaba/kimi/ollama/opencode-go keep identical behavior and are preserved surface (their opt-ins stay untouched, no per-adapter flag proliferation). Per-adapter truncated-stream conformance lives in Task 7 built public-entry tests; base conformance here covers the shared path. Anthropic/Google native streaming adapters are out of scope (preserved). SCOPE AMENDMENT (deviation 2): the strict default rejects simplified [DONE]-only mock streams in the adapter package test files (azure/bedrock/vertex/neuralwatt), which assert a successful done; those four test files are owned here for fixture conformance corrections (finish_reason terminal chunks; harness-only, no adapter source change), so their byte-immutability under the edge-fixes scope does not block the shared default. The edge-fixes item keeps its regression fixtures in NEW dedicated files created at Task 6.

items.title: One dependency-free bounded success-body reader for all non-stream JSON/text endpoints
securityTests: T4 oversized chunked body fully buffers
items.rationale: roadmap 0.2.1 item 2: thirteen confirmed unbounded response.json() success sites (ten model-discovery implementations at models.ts:106/97/92/83/91/102/80/119/83/93, neuralwatt quota.ts:86, alibaba embeddings.ts:88, openai uploads.ts:79). Fix: additive readBoundedResponseJson in src/providers/transport.ts composed on readBoundedResponseText (byte cap DEFAULT_MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_BYTES 65536, depth cap 32, property cap 4096, shape check, abort, redaction) with new ProviderTransportError code response_body_shape; the ten model-discovery files + quota + embeddings migrate here. SCOPE NOTE: packages/provider-openai/src/uploads.ts is claimed by the edge-fixes item (task6) so scopes stay disjoint; task6 performs the uploads success-body migration to the same reader. Per-adapter oversized-body assertions live in Task 7 built public-entry tests; the shared bounds conformance in provider-transport.test.ts covers all thirteen shapes.

items.title: Pin outbound DNS/address decisions for OIDC JWKS, OPA, and content fetches
items.rationale: roadmap 0.2.1 item 3: oidc.ts fetchJwks, opa.ts callOpa, and content media fetches verify the URL string via assertSsrfAllowedUrl + redirect manual but connect to whatever the system resolver returns at connect time (DNS-rebinding/mixed-answer exposure); mcp/src/transport.ts already has the strongest primitive (resolvePinnedAddress 1-32 answers + per-candidate assertSsrfAllowedUrl + requestPinned with a node lookup hook that connects only to the pinned address + 3xx rejection + boundResponse). Fix: lift that algorithm verbatim into new core module src/pinned-fetch.ts (pinnedFetch, MediaContentError ssrf_denied on address violations) and route oidc/opa/content/MCP through it; redirects are REJECTED (roadmap 'disabled' branch, Task 0 decision 6); OIDC key caps, OPA bundle-revision pin/body cap, and content MIME/aggregation policy stay. Task 0 decision 12: packages/coding-security/src/egress/dns-pin.ts is NOT converged (proxy-path primitive, preserved surface).

items.title: Consolidate duplicated OAuth device/token polling and provider parsing
securityTests: T9 OAuth poll drift / unbounded token body / secret leak
items.rationale: roadmap 0.2.1 item 4: provider-openai/src/oauth.ts and credentials-node/src/oauth2.ts duplicate the RFC 8628 device-code poll loop (same SLOW_DOWN_INCREMENT_MS, same TokenSuccessPayload/TokenErrorPayload shapes, same pending/slow_down/expiry/abort/redaction) and both read token success/error bodies unbounded (oauth.ts:150/209/224, oauth2.ts:158/212/226). Fix: one shared bounded pollDeviceCodeToken helper in new core module src/oauth-device-code.ts exported from the core root (verified topology: no provider package depends on credentials-node; both consumers already import from @arnilo/prism), owning the poll loop, backoff, expiry, abort, bounded success reads via readBoundedResponseJson (Task 3 reader), bounded error reads via readBoundedResponseText, redaction, and token-shape parse; provider-specific fields (errorPrefix, accountId, extraTokenParams) stay at the adapters via options. The shared conformance runs against both call sites; microsoft365-oauth.ts/google-workspace-oauth.ts consumers are preserved surface. SCOPE NOTE: docs/credential-storage.md is claimed by the dns-pinning item (task4); the OAuth consolidation docs live in docs/credentials-and-redaction.md here plus the Task 8 migration doc.

items.title: Fix credential, signing, upload, and cache edge cases
securityTests: T12 failed upload DELETE leaks file
items.rationale: roadmap 0.2.1 item 5: four confirmed single-site defects. (a) azure/provider.ts:70+84 and vertex/provider.ts:50+58 resolve options.credential twice per request (outer wrapper + inner apiKey source) - rotating/single-use credentials consumed twice; fix resolve-once with the resolved string injected per request. (b) sigv4.ts:52-60 canonicalHeaders picks the first Object.entries match while duplicate-case keys both survive the spread, and canonicalQuery never sorts repeated keys by value (a===b branch identical) - fix lowercase merge with last-wins (Task 0 decision) and key-then-value query sort; existing fixtures byte-identical. (c) uploads.ts:86-107 cleanup() clears uploadedIds BEFORE the DELETEs so a failed DELETE leaks the file ID - fix remove-on-success only, retain failed IDs for retry cleanup; also migrates the success response.json() (uploads.ts:79) to the Task 3 readBoundedResponseJson (scope note in bounded-success-bodies). (d) cache-telemetry.ts:99-147 overflow bucket applies the current record's model cost to mixed-model overflow tokens - fix tokens-only overflow (no cost fields), Task 0 decision. SCOPE AMENDMENT (deviation 2): the credential-once and signing-canonicalization regression fixtures moved from azure.test.ts/bedrock.test.ts/vertex.test.ts (now owned by the strict-completion item for fixture conformance) into dedicated new test files created at Task 6: credential-once.test.ts (azure + vertex, resolveCredentialValue appears once per request) and sigv4-canonical.test.ts (bedrock duplicate-case headers / repeated query keys). openai.test.ts stays here for the uploads retention regression.

items.title: Public-JavaScript, packed-consumer, and named threat-suite regressions
items.rationale: roadmap mandatory regression matrix items 5-7 and 10-11: the original gaps are runtime-only (truncated streams, unbounded bodies, unpinned connects, duplicated OAuth, double credential consumption, signature mismatches, leaked upload IDs, mixed overflow cost), so regressions must run against BUILT public package entrypoints and a fresh packed plain-JavaScript consumer (install-smoke harness), not private source imports. scripts/phase21-security.test.mjs wires into security:threat-suites (package.json shared-file editor task7); per-adapter truncated-stream and oversized-body assertions for the six OpenAI-compatible adapters and the ten model-discovery paths live here so item scopes stay disjoint (base/source-level conformance lives in Tasks 2-3 files).
